statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). The 1.63% gap-down open has now been fully retraced. The Nasdaq-100 cash index trades 29,185.72, down 0.62%, at roughly 93% of its 28,867.67-29,208.57 session range, and the front-month NQ contract, which rolled to December 2026 today, is quoted 29,491.75 near its own session high. VIX has set a new session low at 16.83, the 10-year has retreated from 5.012% to 4.947% and WTI from $104.79 to $102.72. Tail falls two points to 18 and returns to the low band. The unresolved Saudi East-West pipeline outage remains the outstanding amplifier.
recommendation: Tail at 18 sits in the low band, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The danger window is unchanged at 19:00-20:00 UTC, covering the final cash hour, where conditional Tail peaks at 21, four points below the block mapping. The conditional path stays in the low band across the post-close, overnight and Asian sessions, returns to the watch band during Tuesday's European afternoon, and reaches 22 for the 13:30 UTC cash open. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Gap fully retraced and every amplifier rolls over: NDX presses 93% of its session range while VIX sets a new session low at 16.83, the 10-year falls to 4.947% and WTI to $102.72; Tail eases to 18 and back into the low band, with 19:00-20:00 UTC retained as the danger window
body:
The absorption recorded over the previous two hours has now completed into a full intraday retracement of the opening gap, and every cross-asset amplifier that defined the European morning is decaying at the same time. As of the 16:26 UTC quote, the Nasdaq-100 cash index is at 29,185.72, down 182.72 points or 0.62% against a 29,368.44 close, having opened at 28,890.93 on a 1.63% gap. The session range is 28,867.67 to 29,208.57, which places the index about 93% of the way up that range and within 23 points of its session high. The index has recovered more than 300 points from its low, and that low has now survived roughly six hours spanning the European afternoon, the cash open and three full cash hours. That is a completed and durable retracement, the structural opposite of the repeated extension after failed pullbacks that defines a pathological path.

One methodological note belongs in the public record. The Yahoo and Investing front-month Nasdaq futures quote rolled from the September 2026 contract to December 2026 (NQZ26) during this hour, which shifts the quoted level by roughly 315 points of basis without any corresponding move in the underlying. The December contract is quoted 29,491.75, down 192.50 points or 0.65% against a 29,684.25 close, with a session range of 29,107.25 to 29,505.25, so it sits near 97% of its own range. The percentage change and range position agree closely with the cash index, which is the cross-check used here; the cash index is treated as the primary reference for this assessment precisely because it is continuous across the roll.

The cross-asset picture has moved from amplifying to actively stabilising. VIX is quoted at 16.83, still up 6.25% against a 15.84 close, but it has broken to a new session low of 16.71 after trading as high as 18.17; implied volatility that spikes into a gap-down open and then decays through three cash hours is the signature of an orderly liquidity transfer rather than a disorderly one. The 10-year Treasury yield printed 5.012% earlier today, its first touch of 5% since October 2023, and has since fallen to 4.947%, below its 4.975% previous close and at the low end of a 4.942% to 5.012% range. The 2-year is near 4.62%, essentially unchanged on the session, so the curve move is contained rather than a broad repricing. Crude has done the same: WTI reached $104.79 and Brent $109.44 during the European afternoon and have since eased to $102.72 and $107.29. An amplifier that fails to extend after making its high is no longer contributing to the probability of a no-retracement path.

The catalyst stack itself is unchanged and remains verified from primary reporting. Al Jazeera reports that drones struck Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline on 12 September in two locations near Riyadh and Medina, that the kingdom suspended operations as a precautionary measure, and that the line was carrying roughly four to five million barrels a day, about four to five percent of global supply, to the Red Sea port of Yanbu. Yanbu holds enough stored crude to sustain exports for about five to seven days, while repair estimates range from a partial restart to five or six weeks. Separately, Reuters reports that calls from the heads of Anthropic, OpenAI and xAI for a slower pace of AI model development drove the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down about 6%, its worst day since 1 July, with Nvidia off 3.2% and Intel, AMD and Marvell down 5.6%, 5% and 6.3%.

That semiconductor damage is precisely why the index is not trending. The same Reuters report notes healthcare and consumer staples each up about 1%, Meta and Alphabet both up around 2%, and software higher with ServiceNow, Adobe and Workday gaining 3.8%, 3.6% and 3.2%. The shared cross-asset context file was checked and found stale, collected at 14:26 UTC and therefore beyond the 90-minute freshness limit set by the inherited contract, so it was not used as supporting evidence for this assessment and the seven-day event list and all price levels were verified independently from primary sources. A market in which one industry is down 6% while another is up 3% is dispersing risk internally rather than compressing it into a single direction, and that dispersion belongs in Stress rather than Tail.

The remaining live risks are genuine but they are event risks, not path risks. The pipeline outage is unresolved and physical, so a fresh Gulf headline could reprice crude in any hour. Market pricing for a Federal Reserve rate increase on Wednesday is reported near 90% by Yahoo Finance and at 85.6% on CME FedWatch as of Friday, an unusual configuration that keeps the bond market as the dominant cross-asset channel into midweek. Consistent with the published risk definitions, event importance, surprise magnitude and an unresolved supply mechanism raise Stress and discipline Confidence rather than forcing Tail higher once the observed path shows orderly discovery. Tail therefore falls two points to 18, returning to the low band, and Stress eases two points to 73, still in the high band.

The danger window stays at 19:00 to 20:00 UTC, the final cash hour. It is the remaining scheduled point at which a fully recovered gap-down day either confirms into the settlement or gives the recovery back, and the moment when a late crude headline would meet the thinnest liquidity of the cash session. Conditional Tail peaks at 21 there, four points below the block mapping, reflecting a scheduled transition and the live amplifier count rather than any observed closing structure. Confidence holds at 89: price, volatility, rates, energy, catalyst and calendar evidence is current and verified from primary sources, including the 2-year yield that was missing an hour ago, with the futures contract roll the one discontinuity in the reference series.

lookbackSummary: Over the past 24 hours the Claude series ran through the low band during Sunday's US evening, entered the watch band from 21:00 UTC as the AI-slowdown and Middle East supply stories developed, and reached the elevated band at 09:00 and 10:00 UTC when NQ set a sequence of lower lows under a trend-down mode. It stepped back to the watch band at 11:00 and 12:00 UTC, returned to the elevated band at 13:00 UTC when the first bounce faded into the cash open, then eased steadily through 14:00 and 15:00 UTC as the gap was absorbed. Stress held in the high band throughout, between 71 and 79, and Confidence improved from 71 to 89 as live price evidence became available. All 24 hourly slots are available from published Claude history.
outlookSummary: The 24-hour outlook is built on an opening gap that has been fully retraced while VIX, the 10-year and crude all break back from their session extremes. Conditional Tail holds at 18 through the US midday, edges to 19 into the afternoon and peaks at 21 in the 19:00 UTC power hour that forms the published danger window. It then settles between 17 and 18 across the thin post-close, overnight and Asian sessions, with small uplifts in the hours where crude has typically repriced first on Middle East developments. The path returns to the watch band from Tuesday's European afternoon, reaches 21 for the 12:15 UTC ADP and 12:30 UTC Empire State releases and peaks at 22 for the 13:30 UTC cash open, two points below the block mapping. Confidence declines steadily with distance from the last verified price observation. Every hour beyond the current one is conditional risk, not observed structure.
